papers.digest: This Review introduces a reaction-to-device framework for aqueous zinc-sulfur batteries, linking sulfur conversion chemistry to system-level integration. It evaluates cathodes, electrolytes, mediators, membranes, and zinc interfaces collectively, plus flexible and pouch configurations. This holistic perspective establishes design and benchmarking principles, addressing component interdependence that isolated optimization misses, thereby advancing zinc-sulfur batteries toward safe, economical, scalable energy storage.

This offers a viable strategy for safer lithium metal batteries with thermally triggered fire suppression.

papers.digest: Vacancy-mediated sulfur exchange is identified as a new mechanism accelerating sulfur redox in Li–S batteries. Vacancy density directly correlates with exchange extent and catalysis; it doubles interfacial area and lowers the Li₂S barrier from 0.352 to 0.179 eV, enabling a 504 Wh kg⁻¹ pouch cell.
